data.current_description:
Returns one or more technical indicator lines computed from the asset's close prices.

The requested `window` is widened internally by the indicator's warm-up depth and trimmed back before responding, so the first returned point is already converged rather than carrying seed bias. The window is measured back from the most recent available point, so a feed lagging behind the current time still returns a full window.

`lines` is keyed by line name. Single-line indicators (`sma`, `ema`, `rsi`, `atr`) return one entry named after the indicator. `macd` returns `macd`, `signal` and `histogram`; `bollinger` returns `upper`, `middle`, `lower` and `percent_b`.

`atr` reads OHLC candles rather than closes, so it is only available for assets whose price source stores individual ticks; anything else returns `400`. It is Wilder-smoothed and defaults to a period of 14.

The momentum measures cover fixed spans rather than a caller-supplied `period`, which is rejected for them. `surging_1h`, `surging_4h` and `surging_24h` are the percent price change over that span, so the `resolution` must be coarse enough for the span to fit in 400 buckets — the same bound a supplied `period` carries.
`trending_ratio` is average reported 24h volume over the last 6 hours divided by its 30-day average, so it needs a CoinGecko-mapped asset and a `resolution` of at least `1h`.

VWAP is not offered: it needs per-bucket traded volume, which no price series carries.

data.current_description:
The token endpoint (RFC 6749 4.1.3 and 6), form encoded.

`authorization_code` consumes the code atomically, checks it was issued
to this client and this `redirect_uri`, and verifies PKCE. A code is
single-use: unknown, expired and already-redeemed are one answer, so a
caller cannot tell them apart.

`refresh_token` rotates: the presented token is consumed and the
response carries its replacement, minted with the stored audience and
scopes, so neither can widen on refresh. Refresh tokens are opaque and
single-use; replaying a consumed one revokes every token descended
from the same grant.
data.summary_suggestion: Exchange authorization code or refresh token for access tokens
data.description_suggestion: The OAuth 2.0 token endpoint (RFC 6749 4.1.3 and 6). Accepts form-encoded requests with two grant types: (1) authorization_code: exchanges a single-use authorization code for access and refresh tokens, validating the code was issued to this client and redirect_uri, and verifying PKCE. data.current_description:
Returns one or more technical indicator lines computed from the asset's close prices.

The requested `window` is widened internally by the indicator's warm-up depth and trimmed back before responding, so the first returned point is already converged rather than carrying seed bias. The window is measured back from the most recent available point, so a feed lagging behind the current time still returns a full window.

`lines` is keyed by line name. Single-line indicators (`sma`, `ema`, `rsi`, `atr`) return one entry named after the indicator. `macd` returns `macd`, `signal` and `histogram`; `bollinger` returns `upper`, `middle`, `lower` and `percent_b`.

data.current_description:
The token endpoint (RFC 6749 4.1.3 and 6), form encoded.

`authorization_code` consumes the code atomically, checks it was issued
to this client and this `redirect_uri`, and verifies PKCE. A code is
single-use: unknown, expired and already-redeemed are one answer, so a
caller cannot tell them apart.

`refresh_token` rotates: the presented token is consumed and the
response carries its replacement, minted with the stored audience and
scopes, so neither can widen on refresh. Refresh tokens are opaque and
single-use; replaying a consumed one revokes every token descended
from the same grant.
data.summary_suggestion: Exchange authorization code or refresh token for access tokens
data.description_suggestion: The OAuth 2.0 token endpoint (RFC 6749 4.1.3 and 6). Accepts form-encoded requests with two grant types: (1) authorization_code: exchanges a single-use authorization code for access and refresh tokens, validating the code was issued to this client and redirect_uri, and verifying PKCE. Code is single-use; unknown, expired, and already-redeemed codes return the same error. (2) refresh_token: rotates the refresh token, consuming the presented token and returning its replacement with the same audience and scopes (scopes cannot widen). Refresh tokens are single-use; replaying a consumed token revokes all tokens from that grant.
